rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a multimodal baseline to explore if combining RNA and image data improves performance. This configuration uses simple encoders (pca_n2000, resnet50) with concat fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploration by testing a key design choice (multimodal vs single-modality) while keeping other parameters minimal.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieves 52.66% accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (config_017) improves performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. This is a logical next step to explore a key design choice (fusion) within the multimodal space, balancing exploitation of the current model setting with exploration of critical components.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile setting with the same encoders and aggregation method, isolating the effect of profile setting. It balances exploration of multiprofile (which may improve performance) while maintaining consistency in other components to attribute results to profile setting changes.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings (config_018) outperform singleprofile configurations. This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion in the same multiprofile setup (with avgpool aggregation) can further improve accuracy. It clarifies the impact of fusion methods while maintaining a proven effective configuration, balancing exploitation of promising directions with parameter refinement.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest validation accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) improves performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder while keeping other components consistent. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and avgpool aggregation (config_031) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation, which could improve representation learning for multimodal fusion. It directly isolates the effect of aggregation method on a promising configuration, balancing exploitation of the scvi_n200/resnet50 combination with exploration of transformer's potential for complex interactions.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_033) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests whether using the more advanced imagenet_vit_l image encoder with scgpt RNA encoder (instead of resnet50) further improves performance, isolating the effect of the image encoder while maintaining the proven effective components of transformer aggregation and weighted fusion.

The existing evidence shows config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests the same configuration but with the image encoder changed to imagenet_vit_l, which may offer stronger feature extraction. It clarifies whether the choice of image encoder significantly impacts performance, a critical design choice. This is a logical extension of the current best model, balancing exploitation of promising directions with exploration of key components.

The existing evidence shows config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder and transformer aggregation, which could clarify if the RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs scgpt) impacts performance. It's the best use of the final experiment to explore a key design choice with high potential impact.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (like config_039) achieve high validation accuracy. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion, which isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice while maintaining the effective aggregation/fusion strategy. It directly compares scgpt (a more complex encoder) against scvi_n200 in a setup similar to the current best, helping determine if the RNA encoder choice impacts performance.
